year_style_phases.label: Formative Classic
year_style_phases.title_tendencies: Formal articles ('The X of Y'), character names, epic locations, and highly descriptive, literal phrasing.
year_style_phases.tagline_tendencies: Theatrical, sensational, exclamation-heavy, and narrator-driven promises of unprecedented spectacle.

year_style_phases.label: Gritty Auteur
year_style_phases.title_tendencies: Shorter, punchier, cynical, abstract concepts, and single-word nouns focusing on anti-heroes or urban decay.
year_style_phases.tagline_tendencies: Ominous, character-focused, rhetorical questions, and minimalist existential dread.

year_style_phases.label: High-Concept Blockbuster
year_style_phases.title_tendencies: Action verbs, compound words, explosive adjectives, and easily marketable franchise starters.
year_style_phases.tagline_tendencies: Puns, witty one-liners, star-driven hooks ('[Actor] is...'), and high-stakes ultimatums.

year_style_phases.label: Digital Franchise
year_style_phases.title_tendencies: Heavy use of colons, subtitles, 'The [Noun]', and universe-building keywords indicating a larger lore.
year_style_phases.tagline_tendencies: Epic destiny, 'Everything changes', dark reboots, and cryptic warnings about the future.

year_style_phases.label: Modern Meta
year_style_phases.title_tendencies: Abstract, single words, ironic juxtapositions, highly stylized formatting, and IP-heavy legacy sequels.
year_style_phases.tagline_tendencies: Self-aware, internet-culture adjacent, highly emotional resonance, or deeply ironic subversions of classic tropes.
